meta.purpose: Curated target species for safari planning – not a complete country list.
meta.imagePolicy: Use verifiedPhoto true only for correctly identified species images. Habitat images must set imageRole habitat and must not imply a sighting at a nest site.

species.whyItMatters: Flagship Eastern Arc endemic – shy, forest-floor partridge known only from Udzungwa massif forests.
species.overview: A true forest endemic confined to Udzungwa rainforest. Birds are heard on dawn walks long before they are seen – patience on mossy trails, not stakeouts.
species.identificationNotes: Rotund, rufous-brown forest partridge; walks quietly on forest floor. Voice is the usual field clue.
species.habitatDistribution: Eastern Arc: Udzungwa Mountains National Park and surrounding forest blocks above ~1,200 m.
species.viewingContext: Early morning on park trails with a guide; wet-season mud slows pace. No guaranteed views.

species.whyItMatters: Montane akalat named for the Iringa highlands – a classic Southern Arc list target.
species.overview: Small forest robin-chat of cool highland forest. Often in mixed flocks with other mid-storey species.
species.identificationNotes: Grey-brown above, warm rufous underparts; compare with other akalats by voice and elevation.
species.habitatDistribution: Southern Tanzania highland forest – Mufindi, Udzungwa skirts and related arc patches.
species.viewingContext: Listen-led birding on forest trails; photography needs patience and low light.

images.alt: Southern highlands forest and birding landscape

species.whyItMatters: Striking arc sunbird tied to flowering foothill and montane forest edges.
species.overview: Endemic sunbird often tracked along forest edges and ridges with flowering trees.
species.identificationNotes: Male with rufous wings and green head; forages in canopy and edge.
species.habitatDistribution: Eastern Arc foothills and Kilombero–Udzungwa transition.
species.viewingContext: Best on flowering peaks in dry windows – still weather-dependent.

species.whyItMatters: East Usambara forest endemic – anchor species on northeastern arc modules.
species.overview: Elusive understory akalat of Usambara rainforest – tape and patience, not crowds.
species.identificationNotes: Warm brown akalat; best separated by range and voice from allies.
species.viewingContext: Amani and forest reserves on multi-day northeastern routes.

species.whyItMatters: Kilombero floodplain endemic – wetland focus between forest blocks.
species.overview: Colonial weaver of tall floodplain grasses and wetland edge – pairs with arc forest legs.
species.identificationNotes: Large weaver; male plumage distinct in breeding season.
species.viewingContext: Boat and edge walks when water levels allow – season shapes access.

images.alt: Southern Tanzania wetland and floodplain birding

species.whyItMatters: Critically endangered lark confined to Lark Plains near Arusha – a measured northern add-on.
species.overview: Grassland lark with a tiny global range. Visits are short, respectful and guide-led.
species.identificationNotes: Large lark of short-grass plains; structure and display flight aid ID.
species.habitatDistribution: Lark Plains grassland near Arusha – not a general serengeti species.
species.viewingContext: Morning on the plains with a local guide; no flushing for photography.

images.alt: Arusha region plains and montane backdrop

species.whyItMatters: Island endemic owl – Pemba module on long national endemic tours.
species.overview: Nocturnal island endemic located by call in forest and plantations – not diurnal ticking.
species.identificationNotes: Small scops-owl; identification by voice and brief night views.
species.habitatDistribution: Pemba Island forests and wooded mosaics.
species.viewingContext: Night walks with guide; respectful playback policies apply.

species.whyItMatters: Seasonal forest-floor jewel on eastern and western forest routes – timing matters.
species.overview: Migratory pitta on passage and breeding – brief windows, not year-round.
species.identificationNotes: Unmistakable when seen; often located by display call at dawn.
species.habitatDistribution: Eastern and western Tanzania forests in season – not guaranteed on every departure.
species.viewingContext: Wet-season dawn listening in forest; no nest or stakeout detail published.
